old.design_population: European Liver Transplant Registry: 105 recipients with unresectable HCC in noncirrhotic livers.
old.selection: Transplantation as primary treatment (62) or for intrahepatic recurrence after resection (43).
old.results: Lymph-node involvement (HR 2.60) and macrovascular invasion (HR 2.55) were independently associated with death; five-year survival 59% without either.
old.limits: Noncirrhotic population; nodal status as recorded by centres, not previously treated nodal disease.

new.design_population: European Liver Transplant Registry cohort of 105 recipients with unresectable HCC in noncirrhotic livers across 38 centers.
new.selection: 62 received a primary transplant and 43 underwent transplant for intrahepatic recurrence after resection. Transplant pathology identified hilar nodal involvement in 12 of 105 recipients.
new.results: Five-year overall survival after transplant was 17% with positive hilar nodes (95% CI 0–38%) and 54% with negative nodes (43–64%). The adjusted hazard ratio for death with positive nodes was 2.60 (95% CI 1.28–5.28).
new.limits: Prior resection pathology was unavailable for the 43 rescue transplants. Survival after documented clearance of previously proven nodal metastases was not reported.
new.locator: J Hepatol. 2012;57:297–305. Pathology p. 298, Table 1 p. 300, Fig. 2C p. 302, Table 3 p. 303, Table 4 and prior resection pathology p. 304.

edits.old: Every HCC transplant framework reviewed requires absence of extrahepatic disease, and AASLD lists lymph-node involvement or extrahepatic spread as downstaging failure and an exclusion from transplantation. ILTS–ILCA recommends downstaging, and immunotherapy for downstaging, only in patients without extrahepatic disease, and the XXL trial excluded extrahepatic spread, including hepatic-hilum nodes with a short axis >2 cm. Lymph-node involvement was strongly adverse after transplantation (HR 2.60 for death in noncirrhotic livers; pooled odds ratio 10.44 for recurrence with positive hilar nodes). A complete response is not cure: among 160 complete responders to immunotherapy-based treatment, prior extrahepatic metastasis doubled the risk of recurrence (adjusted HR 2.00), and 5-year recurrence-free survival in the whole cohort was 18%. The only published transplant after metastatic HCC is one case: the best response of nodal, lung and bone disease to nivolumab was partial, the bone lesions did not clearly regress, liver disease recurred off treatment and was ablated, extrahepatic clearance was never confirmed by biopsy or PET, and the recipient was free of cancer one year after transplantation.
edits.new: Every HCC transplant framework reviewed requires absence of extrahepatic disease, and AASLD lists lymph-node involvement or extrahepatic spread as downstaging failure and an exclusion from transplantation. ILTS–ILCA recommends downstaging, and immunotherapy for downstaging, only in patients without extrahepatic disease, and the XXL trial excluded extrahepatic spread, including hepatic-hilum nodes with a short axis >2 cm. In noncirrhotic HCC, five-year survival was 17% with positive hilar nodes at transplant and 54% with negative nodes. A separate meta-analysis found higher odds of recurrence with positive hilar nodes (pooled OR 10.44). Neither study establishes outcomes after prior proven nodal disease cleared. A complete response is not cure: among 160 complete responders to immunotherapy-based treatment, prior extrahepatic metastasis doubled the risk of recurrence (adjusted HR 2.00), and 5-year recurrence-free survival in the whole cohort was 18%. The only published transplant after metastatic HCC is one case: the best response of nodal, lung and bone disease to nivolumab was partial, the bone lesions did not clearly regress, liver disease recurred off treatment and was ablated, extrahepatic clearance was never confirmed by biopsy or PET, and the recipient was free of cancer one year after transplantation.

edits.old: Keep closed. Previous extrahepatic metastasis is outside the standard pathway and every HCC high-risk cohort, even after local treatment or a complete response to immunotherapy. Record durable complete responders in a registry; this edition offers no transplant route.
edits.new: The local draft keeps standard and high-risk transplant routes closed after proven extrahepatic or nodal HCC, including after a complete response. Enroll durable complete responders in a prospective follow-up registry.
